name: agentegress
description: See which AI agent and MCP server is talking to what on this Windows PC, and check it for signs of compromise.
long_description:
agentegress walks the live process tree from each AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, ...) down to the MCP servers and scripts it started, attributes every TCP connection and listener, and checks the PC for signs of compromise: unsigned programs talking out or listening, autostarts, firewall, Remote Desktop.

The verdict comes from deterministic rules, not from the model. Everything read from the machine is returned under `untrusted` keys, and text that tries to instruct an AI is reported as a finding. Read-only; it opens no network connection of its own. The tool results (process names, paths, command lines with known credential formats masked, connection addresses) are sent to your model provider as part of the conversation, like any tool output.

tools.name: scan_summary
tools.description: Scan this PC and return the rule-based verdict, the findings that must be reported, the running AI agents with their MCP servers, and what could not be checked.

tools.name: list_findings
tools.description: Every finding from the rules, most severe first.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: Process trees of running AI agents with the MCP servers they started and each process's network connections.

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: Established TCP connections with the owning process and the organisation behind the peer address when known.

tools.name: explain_process
tools.description: Signature, ancestry, children, connections, findings and autostarts for one process.

tools.name: list_listening_ports
tools.description: Processes accepting TCP connections on a network interface.

tools.name: list_autostarts
tools.description: Run keys, Startup folder items, services, scheduled tasks and Winlogon values, with signature status.

tools.name: login_activity
tools.description: Failed and Remote Desktop logons from the last 24 hours (needs administrator rights).
